result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure and poorly maintained, overgrown sidewalks. The wide roadway and presence of parked vehicles on both sides create potential visibility issues and encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential setting.

hazards.name: Overgrown Vegetation
hazards.description: Bushes and weeds are encroaching on the narrow sidewalk on the left, forcing pedestrians closer to the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and midground along the property line.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked places for pedestrians to cross the street safely between residential blocks.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A line of parked cars on the right side of the street can hide pedestrians from oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearing and Repair
interventions.description: Clear overgrown vegetation and repair the sidewalk surface to provide a clear, accessible path for all users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at intersections to define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines.

result.summary: The environment is a wide, unmarked roadway adjacent to a public park and playground, lacking basic pedestrian crossing infrastructure. Parked vehicles and mature trees create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians, particularly children, attempting to cross the street.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: No designated or marked crossing point exists for pedestrians to access the adjacent park and playground.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire roadway foreground

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, especially children, who might step into the road.
hazards.location_in_image: Curb line where the blue and black cars are parked

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the asphalt roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility (continental style) marked crosswalk to designate a safe crossing point to the park.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the crossing point to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Pedestrian Crossing' warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of people crossing to the playground.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is primarily residential and lacks basic safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and a continuous sidewalk network. Pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic due to the absence of walkways on one side and sightline obstructions from overgrown vegetation and parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Discontinuous Sidewalk Network
hazards.description: The sidewalk is only present on one side of the street and does not appear to be a continuous public network, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway and foreground.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, providing no designated space for pedestrians to cross and no visual cue for drivers to expect them.
hazards.location_in_image: Center intersection area.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large bush on the corner and a parked van on the shoulder block visibility between pedestrians and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right corner vegetation and left side parked van.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Install continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark the intersection with high-visibility crosswalks and install corresponding curb ramps to improve safety and accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Trim the large bush at the corner and implement parking restrictions near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a residential dead-end street with a narrow sidewalk on the right side and no marked pedestrian infrastructure. While the 'No Outlet' sign suggests low traffic volumes, the lack of crossings, curb ramps, and poor pavement quality reduces overall pedestrian safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: Pedestrians crossing the street have no designated or protected space, increasing exposure to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible roadway

hazards.name: Overgrown vegetation
hazards.description: Bushes on the right side may obstruct sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Pavement degradation
hazards.description: Cracks and uneven surfaces in the roadway could pose a trip hazard or affect vehicle handling.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground of the asphalt

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at logical crossing points to improve pedestrian visibility and define right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps at crossing points to ensure accessibility for all users, including those with mobility aids.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim back overgrown bushes to improve sightlines and ensure the full width of the sidewalk is usable.
